name: Microsoft Entra ID
tagline: Cloud identity and access management for users, groups, apps and Azure.
whatItIs: Microsoft's cloud-based identity service (formerly Azure Active Directory). It stores users, groups, devices, applications and service principals, and authenticates sign-ins to Azure, Microsoft 365 and thousands of SaaS apps.
primaryPurpose: Authenticate identities and provide the directory that Azure RBAC, Conditional Access and app access rely on.
useCases: Single sign-on to Azure and SaaS apps
Hybrid identity with on-premises Active Directory
security: Use PIM for just-in-time admin roles
Limit Global Administrators and monitor sign-in/audit logs
networking: Cloud service reached over the internet; Conditional Access can restrict by named locations/IPs
pricing: Free tier included with Azure subscriptions; premium capabilities (P1, P2, Governance) are licensed per user.

confusedWith.name: Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS)
confusedWith.difference: AD DS is on-premises Kerberos/LDAP; Entra ID is a cloud identity service using modern protocols (OAuth, OIDC, SAML).

confusedWith.name: Microsoft Entra Domain Services
confusedWith.difference: A managed domain providing LDAP/Kerberos/Group Policy for legacy apps in Azure; Entra ID itself doesn't offer domain join of servers in that classic sense.

relevanceNote: Users, groups, licenses, guests, SSPR and the relationship to Azure RBAC are directly tested.
examTips: Dynamic groups and group-based licensing require P1+
A license can't be assigned without a usage location

name: Management Groups
tagline: Organize subscriptions into a hierarchy for governance at scale.
whatItIs: Containers above subscriptions that let you apply Azure Policy and RBAC to many subscriptions at once. Every tenant has a root management group.
primaryPurpose: Apply consistent governance across many subscriptions.
useCases: Enterprise landing zones (Platform, Landing zones, Sandbox)
Assigning auditors Reader across all subscriptions
keyFeatures: Hierarchy up to six levels deep below the root
Default management group for new subscriptions
Single parent per subscription and management group
security: Restrict who can create management groups and move subscriptions (hierarchy settings)
Assign broad roles carefully — they inherit to everything below

confusedWith.name: Resource groups
confusedWith.difference: Resource groups contain resources inside a subscription; management groups contain subscriptions.

confusedWith.name: Administrative units
confusedWith.difference: AUs scope Entra directory roles over users/groups; management groups scope Azure governance over subscriptions.

relevanceNote: Configuring management groups and understanding inheritance is in the skills outline.
examTips: Assign at a management group to cover all current and future subscriptions under it
A subscription can be in only one management group

name: Azure Policy
tagline: Enforce rules on resource configuration and report compliance.
whatItIs: A service that evaluates resources against policy definitions and initiatives, then denies, audits, modifies or deploys configuration to keep resources compliant.
primaryPurpose: Guardrails and compliance at scale, regardless of who deploys resources.
useCases: Deploy diagnostic settings or agents automatically
keyFeatures: Effects: Deny, Audit, Append, Modify, DeployIfNotExists, AuditIfNotExists, Disabled
security: Remediation uses a managed identity — grant it only the roles it needs
Use Deny for hard guardrails and Audit while piloting
networking: Can enforce network settings, e.g., deny public IPs or require private endpoints
pricing: No charge for Azure resources (some guest configuration features may be billed).

confusedWith.name: Azure RBAC
confusedWith.difference: RBAC grants permissions to principals; Policy constrains resource properties for everyone.

confusedWith.name: Resource locks
confusedWith.difference: Locks block delete/modify of specific resources; Policy evaluates configurations.

relevanceNote: Implementing and managing Azure Policy is an explicit AZ-104 skill.
examTips: Existing resources need a remediation task

name: Microsoft Cost Management
tagline: Analyze, budget and optimize cloud spending.
whatItIs: Tools in the Azure portal to view costs, forecast spending, allocate costs with tags, and create budgets with alerts.
primaryPurpose: Visibility and control over Azure spend.
useCases: Monthly budgets per subscription or resource group
keyFeatures: Cost analysis with grouping and forecasts
Budgets with actual and forecasted alert thresholds
security: Access controlled by RBAC (Cost Management Reader/Contributor) and billing roles
pricing: No charge for Azure usage analysis.

confusedWith.name: Spending limit
confusedWith.difference: Only on certain offers; disables resources at the limit. Budgets just alert (and can trigger automation).

relevanceNote: Managing costs with alerts, budgets and Advisor recommendations is in the outline.
examTips: Budgets don't stop resources by themselves
Use forecasted-cost alerts to warn early

name: Azure Advisor
whatItIs: A free service that analyzes your configuration and usage and recommends improvements across Cost, Security, Reliability, Operational Excellence and Performance.
primaryPurpose: Find and act on optimization opportunities.
useCases: Right-size or shut down underused VMs
security: Security recommendations come from Microsoft Defender for Cloud

confusedWith.name: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
confusedWith.difference: Defender for Cloud is the security posture/threat protection service; Advisor surfaces its recommendations alongside cost, reliability and performance ones.

relevanceNote: Named in the cost management skill.
examTips: 'Identify underutilized VMs to reduce cost' → Azure Advisor

name: Azure Key Vault
tagline: Secure storage for secrets, keys and certificates.
whatItIs: A managed service for storing and controlling access to secrets, cryptographic keys and certificates, with HSM-backed options.
primaryPurpose: Keep secrets and keys out of code and centrally control access to them.
useCases: Customer-managed keys for Storage and disks
TLS certificates for App Service and Application Gateway
keyFeatures: Access via Azure RBAC (recommended) or vault access policies
security: Enable purge protection for CMK scenarios
Use managed identities to access secrets
Restrict network access with private endpoints
networking: Firewall with VNet rules and trusted services; private endpoints
pricing: Per operation and per key type (software vs HSM-protected); certificates renewals may be charged.

confusedWith.name: Storage account keys
confusedWith.difference: Account keys grant storage access; Key Vault can store and rotate them.

relevanceNote: Appears in encryption (ADE, CMK) and certificate scenarios.
examTips: ADE requires the vault in the same region and subscription as the VM with disk encryption enabled for the vault
